Answer Part 2: Spec DD (Specification-Driven Development)

Contract specification link: docs/lab-04/specification.md. Written and merged via PR #30 (commit d3793ca) before any implementation branch began.

2.1 Sprint Goal & Stakeholder Request

Sprint Goal: Deliver a production-grade operational service desk workflow by adding multi-action tracking per ticket, enforcing robust state transition and resolution rules, providing role-tailored dashboards for Requesters and IT Staff, and verifying total regression stability across all 4 labs.

Stakeholder Interpretation: Move TokTickIT from a basic communication channel into an enterprise work management system. IT Staff must be able to log concrete operational actions with dates, descriptions, results, and follow-up flags. The ticket status workflow must guarantee that no ticket is resolved without a responsible owner, and dashboards must summarize key operational metrics with direct drill-downs to filtered queues.

2.2 Numbered Functional Requirements (FR)

  • FR-01: Actions Taken Data Model — 1-to-many relationship between Ticket and ActionsTaken.
  • FR-02: Action Creation — IT Staff/Admin can create an action; performer is auto-stamped from active session.
  • FR-03: Action Editing — IT Staff can edit action fields; original creation timestamp and performer are immutable.
  • FR-04: Follow-up Flag & Conditional Note — When followUpRequired is true, followUpNote is mandatory.
  • FR-05: Requester Visibility — Requesters see all actions on their own tickets in clean read-only mode.
  • FR-06: Permitted Status Transitions — Frontend and backend strictly enforce permitted transitions between the 8 statuses.
  • FR-07: Resolution Gate — Transitions to RESOLVED or CLOSED require an assigned ticket owner.
  • FR-08: Stale-Update Conflict Protection — Concurrency detection using expectedCurrentStatus; returns 409 Conflict if mismatched.
  • FR-09: Requester Advisory Flag Reset — Moving status clears requesterConfirmedResolved to avoid misleading states.
  • FR-10: Requester Dashboard — Displays My Open Tickets, Waiting on Me, Resolved Tickets, and 5 recent tickets.
  • FR-11: IT Staff Dashboard — Displays Unassigned, Assigned to Me, Waiting for Requester, High Priority, breakdowns, and recent 5 tickets.
  • FR-12: Zen Green UI Polish & Accessibility — Fully responsive (375px mobile, 768px tablet, 1280px desktop) with WCAG AA compliance.

2.3 Permitted Ticket Status Transition Matrix

Current Status Permitted Next Statuses Authorized Roles Special Rules / Constraints
NEW OPEN, CANCELLED IT Staff, Admin Initial state upon requester creation
OPEN IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_FOR_REQUESTER, RESOLVED, CANCELLED IT Staff, Admin Resolution requires assigned ticket owner (BR-14)
IN_PROGRESS WAITING_FOR_REQUESTER, RESOLVED, CANCELLED IT Staff, Admin Resolution dialog confirmation; owner required (BR-14)
WAITING_FOR_REQUESTER IN_PROGRESS, RESOLVED, CANCELLED IT Staff, Admin Requester advisory button flags ticket as appearing resolved
RESOLVED CLOSED, REOPENED IT Staff, Admin Requester can reopen or confirm resolved; staff can close
CLOSED REOPENED IT Staff, Admin Terminal lifecycle state; reopenable on renewed incident
REOPENED IN_PROGRESS, RESOLVED, CANCELLED IT Staff, Admin Resets confirmation flag (BR-15)
CANCELLED None (Terminal) IT Staff, Admin Ticket cancelled; no further transitions allowed

2.4 Key Business Rules & Dashboard Calculations

  • BR-01 & BR-02 (Parent-Child & Assignee Independence): An Action Taken belongs to exactly 1 ticket. The Ticket Owner coordinates the ticket, but any authorized IT Staff member may record actions.
  • BR-04 & BR-10 (Performer Immutability): The performedById field is strictly stamped by the backend session and cannot be tampered with. Updates preserve original performer and creation timestamp.
  • BR-14 (Resolution Gate): A ticket cannot transition to RESOLVED or CLOSED if ownerId === null (HTTP 400 with TICKET_MUST_BE_ASSIGNED_BEFORE_RESOLUTION).
  • BR-16 (Stale-Update Conflict): Status updates accept expectedCurrentStatus. If the database status differs, HTTP 409 Conflict is returned with the current ticket state.
  • BR-17 (Requester Scoping): Requester dashboard only queries tickets where requesterId === session.userId.
  • BR-18 (Staff Metrics): Staff dashboard calculates unassigned tickets (ownerId: null, status: NOT IN (RESOLVED, CLOSED, CANCELLED)) and user-assigned tickets dynamically.

Answer Part 5: Working IT Staff Dashboard UI

5.1 Dashboard Features & Database Query Evidence

The IT Staff Dashboard (GET /api/dashboard/staff) acts as the operational command center for service desk engineers. It aggregates live data from the database using authoritative Prisma queries and provides 1-click drill-downs into filtered views:

  • Unassigned Tickets Metric: prisma.ticket.count({ where: { ownerId: null, status: { notIn: ['RESOLVED', 'CLOSED', 'CANCELLED'] } } }) → Links directly to /staff/queue?filter=unassigned.
  • My Assigned Tickets Metric: prisma.ticket.count({ where: { ownerId: userId, status: { notIn: ['RESOLVED', 'CLOSED', 'CANCELLED'] } } }) → Links to /staff/queue?filter=mine.
  • Waiting for Requester: prisma.ticket.count({ where: { status: 'WAITING_FOR_REQUESTER' } }) → Links to /staff/queue?status=WAITING_FOR_REQUESTER.
  • High / Urgent Priority: prisma.ticket.count({ where: { itPriority: { in: ['HIGH', 'URGENT'] }, status: { notIn: ['RESOLVED', 'CLOSED', 'CANCELLED'] } } }).
  • Status & Priority Breakdown: Grouped badge distribution showing counts for all active ticket states.
  • Administrator Metric: prisma.user.count({ where: { active: true } }) — Shown exclusively for Administrators.
  • Recent Tickets Table: Displays the 5 most recently updated tickets with priority badges, status chips, requester names, and direct links to Ticket Detail.

Answer Part 6: Working Actions Taken UI

6.1 Multi-Action Lifecycle & Role Enforcement

The Actions Taken module (client/src/components/ActionsTaken.tsx) provides a complete work log directly within the Ticket Detail screen:

  • Action Listing: Chronological cards displaying creation timestamp, performer name, action description, and result.
  • Performer Immutability (BR-04): The performer is automatically stamped from the authenticated session (req.session.userId); users cannot spoof or alter the performer.
  • Follow-up Flag & Conditional Note (FR-04): When "Follow-up required" is checked, an amber badge is displayed on the action card and the "Follow-up Note" field becomes strictly mandatory.
  • Role-Based Security:
    • IT Staff & Admin: Full action creation and editing capabilities; "Log Action" button and inline forms are accessible.
    • Requester: Strict read-only presentation; creation, editing, and internal controls are omitted, but action history is visible to keep the requester informed.

Answer Part 7: Working Ticket Workflow

7.1 Workflow Rules, Resolution Gate & Concurrency

Sprint 4 establishes ironclad ticket lifecycle controls enforced by both frontend guards and backend validation:

  • Permitted Transition Options: The status selector dynamically computes permitted next statuses based on the ticket's current state (e.g. OPEN → IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_FOR_REQUESTER, RESOLVED, CANCELLED). Unlisted transitions are disallowed.
  • Resolution Gate (BR-14): When transitioning to RESOLVED or CLOSED, the backend verifies that ownerId !== null. If unassigned, the request is rejected with HTTP 400 and code TICKET_MUST_BE_ASSIGNED_BEFORE_RESOLUTION.
  • Resolution Confirmation Modal: Transitioning to RESOLVED displays an accessible confirmation dialog requiring the staff member to verify that all actions taken are complete and documented.
  • Stale Update Conflict Detection (BR-16): Every status update submits expectedCurrentStatus. If another engineer updated the status in the interim, the backend returns HTTP 409 Conflict with a conflict banner in the UI prompting the user to refresh.
  • Requester Advisory Reset (BR-15): If a requester previously clicked "Problem Appears Resolved", any subsequent status transition automatically resets requesterConfirmedResolved = false.

Answer Part 8: Working Requester Dashboard and Final Regression UI

8.1 Requester Dashboard & User Scoping

The Requester Dashboard (GET /api/dashboard/requester) provides requesters with a dedicated summary of their tickets:

  • Strict Isolation (BR-17): Queries are hard-scoped to req.session.userId. A requester cannot access or aggregate data from any other user.
  • Concise Metric Cards: "My Open Tickets", "Waiting on Me" (needs requester response), and "Resolved Tickets".
  • Drill-down Navigation: Clicking "View All" on any card opens the My Tickets screen with corresponding filters.
  • Recent Tickets: Displays the 5 most recent tickets submitted by the requester, with live status pills and timestamps.
